mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and rise in unemployment rate signals a broad-based economic slowdown that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with declining HOUST and rising UNRATE, or interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in regression model.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL above 2.5% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve tightens policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production indicates strengthening manufacturing activity and economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with rising INDPRO, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 1200 thousand units, it signals strong consumer demand for housing and associated economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 1200, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market boom regime (HOUST above 1200 thousand units), sustained high demand fuels economic growth and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with HOUST > 1200, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth combined with low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy supporting supply expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with rising INDPRO and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or interaction term is not significant (p>0.05) in regression model.
